name: Ospemifene pivotal studies
question: Does oral ospemifene improve vaginal atrophy findings and bothersome dryness or dyspareunia compared with placebo in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women with at most 5% superficial vaginal cells, vaginal pH above 5.0, and at least one moderate or severe symptom of vulvovaginal atrophy.
design.locator: Full text, Methods and Table 1, pp 481–482

verdictNote: All coprimary comparisons met at 60 mg; 30 mg missed dyspareunia.
takeaway: In the 826-woman Bachmann trial, oral ospemifene 60 mg daily improved vaginal cytology and pH in the full cohort and dryness and dyspareunia in the respective most-bothersome-symptom subgroups versus placebo at 12 weeks; 30 mg missed the dyspareunia comparison.

delivery.value: Oral ospemifene 30 or 60 mg each morning or placebo for 12 weeks; all participants received nonhormonal vaginal lubricant for use as needed. In the final week, lubricant was used by 22% at 60 mg, 31% at 30 mg, and 29% with placebo.
